title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 19: lower bound on the largest induced bipartite subgraph size from average eccentricity and neighborhood independence
abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Conjecture 19 from E. DeLaVina's Written on the Wall II (Graffiti.pc) collection, matching the exact statement in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture19.conjecture19). For every finite, nontrivial, connected simple graph G, the size b(G) of a largest induced bipartite subgraph is bounded below by the floor of the sum of the average vertex eccentricity and the maximum local neighborhood independence number sup_v l(v). The proof picks a vertex u maximising l(u), sets e = (G.eccent u).toNat and D = G.diam, and constructs an induced bipartite subgraph as a disjoint union of independent subsets B_d inside the distance spheres {v | G.dist u v = d} colored by distance parity. When D ≤ e, one geodesic vertex per sphere 2 ≤ d ≤ e together with {u} and an independent neighborhood subset I ⊆ N(u) of size l(u) gives b(G) ≥ e + l(u). When e < D, the average eccentricity is strictly less than D, and pairing geodesic vertices from u toward a diametral pair x, y on overlapping spheres (separated by distance at least 2 via the triangle inequality) gives b(G) ≥ D − 1 + l(u). The proof uses only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, with no sorry and no native_decide.
